dct_description_sm: The Provincial Land Use Atlas (LUA) is a collection of digital land use data displaying administrative boundaries, proposed/approved developments, and layers associated with land use policies/regulations/legislation. The LUA was originally created as a tool to process Crown land applications and an aide in resource planning to identify potential land use conflicts. Included with the LUA is topographic base-mapping, aerial photography, imagery, Crown Land titles/applications, Municipal Plans and land use/land use restriction data.
dct_rights_sm: The Crown Lands issued titles (Grants, Leases, etc.) do not include all privately held land. The Crown Lands Registry does not contain information on all land ownership within the Province and the information depicted cannot be considered complete. The boundary lines shown are intended to be used as an index and the accuracy may not be sufficient for measurement purposes. Crown lands Grants show only the original title holder and Crown Lands does not track subsequent land sales. Provincial and municipal designation and zoning classifications and requirements (including, but not limited to, municipal and provincial land use plans and regulations) are amended on a regular basis. Municipal Zoning information contained within this mapping application has been generalized for display purposes. All new planning documents must be registered with the Department of Municipal Affairs and Environment, where official legal versions are kept on file. For more complete and up to date information users should consult the Registry of Land Use Plans and Development Regulations - https://www.gov.nl.ca/eccm/registry/
